name: The Bitch
description: The Bitch is a Seven Card Stud poker variant where the Queen of Spades (the 'Bitch') is a game-disrupting card. history.origins: The Bitch is part of the family of Seven Card Stud variants that add special 'kill card' mechanics, alongside games like Chicago, Follow the Queen, and Black Mariah. These variants emerged from American home poker games where players sought to add drama and unpredictability to standard stud.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Seven Card Stud variants with special card mechanics become popular in American home games.
Late 20th century: The Bitch, along with Chicago and Black Mariah, becomes a staple of dealer's-choice home poker nights.
Present: Primarily a home/casual game â€” rarely played in casinos.
history.cultural: A quintessential American home poker variant. The name reflects the frustration of having your hand killed when the Qâ™  appears face-up. The split-pot mechanic rewards both strong hands and the luck of holding the Qâ™  in the hole.
history.evolution: Part of the broader trend of adding 'chaos cards' to stud poker to create dramatic moments. The Qâ™  as a kill card that resets the deal creates unique tension every time a queen appears on the board.

setup.dealing: Standard Seven Card Stud deal: 2 cards face-down (hole cards), then cards dealt face-up one at a time with betting rounds between each. 7 cards total per player (2 down, 4 up, 1 down).

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the best 5-card poker hand at showdown, OR by holding the Queen of Spades in the hole.
rules.gameplay: Ante up. Dealer gives two hole cards face-down and one face-up (third street), then a betting round. Then four more cards are dealt face-up one at a time with a betting round after each (fourth through seventh street). If the Queen of Spades is ever dealt face-up, the hand is killed: cards are thrown in, reshuffled, and redealt to players who had not folded. At showdown, best 5-card hand splits the pot with the player holding Queen of Spades in the hole (if any); if Queen of Spades was never dealt, best hand wins the whole pot.
keyRules: Qâ™  dealt face-up = KILL. Hand stops immediately. Reshuffle and redeal to remaining players.
Qâ™  in the hole (face-down) at showdown = split the pot with the best hand.
If Qâ™  is never dealt at all, best hand wins entire pot.
Players who folded before the kill are eliminated from the redeal.

strategy.basic: Standard Seven Card Stud fundamentals: play strong starting hands, fold weak ones early. If you have the Qâ™  in the hole, you're guaranteed half the pot at showdown â€” play aggressively.
strategy.intermediate: The Qâ™  face-up kill creates an incentive to stay in the hand longer â€” if a redeal occurs, you get a fresh chance with a smaller field. Players who fold early lose this option. However, don't chase the redeal with terrible cards.
strategy.advanced: Qâ™  in the hole is essentially a free split pot â€” use it to build the pot aggressively since you're guaranteed at least half. If you have both a strong hand AND Qâ™  in the hole, you can win the entire pot. Watch the board: if all queens have appeared face-up or in mucked hands, no one can hold Qâ™  in the hole.
tips: Holding Qâ™  in the hole is gold â€” you're guaranteed half the pot minimum. Bet and raise aggressively.
If the Qâ™  hasn't appeared by 6th street, it could be in someone's hole cards. Factor this into your pot-splitting evaluation.
Don't fold too early â€” staying in preserves your chance to benefit from a kill/redeal.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Seven Card Stud variant where the Queen of Spades is the 'Bitch.' If she's dealt face-up, the hand is killed and redealt. If she's hiding in your hole cards, you split the pot with the best hand. Hold her. Hide her. Profit.
